# `line-length`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: `max-columns`, `allow-unsplittable`

Reports source lines wider than the configured number of display columns.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`zig fmt` cannot wrap every string, comment, or chained expression, so a project
limit needs a separate policy check.

## When it fires

Columns are counted as a terminal shows them: a tab advances to the next
multiple of eight, East Asian wide characters and emoji take two columns,
combining marks none, and a CRLF line ending is not part of the line. With
`allow-unsplittable`, a line that cannot be wrapped is exempt: one naming a URL,
one token without whitespace, a line of a `\\` multiline string (splitting it
changes the string), or a line holding only a string literal, followed at most
by `,`, `;`, `++` or closing delimiters. A string after other code is reported,
since it can move to a line of its own.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const message = "this string literal is deliberately long so that the whole declaration line goes past one hundred columns";
```

## Options

Set these in the rule's object in `zig-analyzer.json`, next to `level`:

```json
{
  "lints": {
    "rules": {
      "line-length": {
        "level": "warning",
        "max-columns": 100,
        "allow-unsplittable": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- `max-columns` (default `100`): the longest allowed line in columns, a positive
  integer.
- `allow-unsplittable` (default `true`): whether a line that cannot be split,
  such as one long string literal, is exempt, a boolean.
